answer: An agent economy can allocate contract votes in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than counting identities. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize a large share of the stake, losing access to that capital. Like a glacier feeding a reef, influence follows a measurable resource; fresh accounts offer no haven from its cost.
